title: Implicit Semantics
summary: The meaning of data exists only implicitly in column names, application code or people's heads, instead of in governed definitions.
body_markdown:
# Implicit Semantics

## Problem

Data meaning is inferred from names (`status`, `date1`, `klant_type`) and code, never stated.

## Symptoms

- Recurring discussions about "what this field really means".
- Two reports with the same KPI name and different numbers.
- Migration mappings based on column names only.

## Root Causes

- Delivery pressure; no semantic role; modeling starts at the physical layer ([[Physical-Model-First Design]]).

## Consequences

- Integration errors, misreporting, costly migrations, regulatory risk.

## Detection

- Sample columns of key tables: can a definition, owner and concept link be found for each? Coverage below an agreed threshold indicates the anti-pattern.

## Remediation

- Introduce governed [[Business Concept|concepts]] for high-value data first; link models ([[Concept-to-Model Traceability]]); require definitions in [[Data Contract|data contracts]].

## Alternative Patterns

[[Concept-to-Model Traceability]], [[Data Contract]].

## When It May Be Acceptable

Local, short-lived data with a single producer and consumer.
